title: The 10 Best HVLP Paint Sprayers
subtitle: Electric HVLP paint and stain sprayers for furniture, cabinets, fences and walls, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An HVLP sprayer atomizes paint with a high volume of low-pressure air, giving a smooth finish with less overspray than an airless sprayer. We ranked 10 best-sellers from HomeRight, Wagner, Fuji Spray, Graco and budget brands on rating, review volume and features (spraying unthinned paint, a separate turbine base, brass nozzles and flow control). Cheap handhelds need thinned paint; the turbine systems give the finest finish.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: HomeRight Super Finish Max HVLP Paint and Stain Sprayer, 3 Brass Tips

specs.extras: Needs less thinning than the Finish Max

products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed sprayer here: a handheld HVLP with three brass tips and two air caps for furniture, cabinets, fences and decks. It needs less thinning than HomeRight's older Finish Max but isn't sold as an unthinned sprayer.
products.best_for: DIYers refinishing furniture, cabinets, fences and decks.
products.skip_if: You want to spray paint straight from the can.

products.name: VONFORN Paint Sprayer, 700W Spray Paint Gun with 4 Nozzles and 3 Patterns
products.verdict: A cheap handheld sprayer with four nozzle sizes, three patterns, a flow knob and a dust-blowing attachment to clean surfaces before spraying.
products.best_for: Small DIY jobs on a tight budget.
products.skip_if: You don't want to thin paint; plan on it with this type.

products.name: Wagner Spraytech FLEXiO 595 Handheld HVLP Paint and Stain Sprayer

specs.controls: 9 power settings, variable flow, adjustable width and pattern

products.verdict: Wagner's handheld that sprays unthinned interior and exterior paints and stains through its iSpray nozzle, with nine power settings and a second nozzle for detail work. Wagner says it covers an 8x10 wall in 5 minutes.
products.best_for: Painting walls, ceilings and siding without thinning.
products.skip_if: You want the finest cabinet finish; a turbine system like Fuji does better.
pros: Two nozzles for walls and detail
cons: Heavy in the hand when full

products.name: Fuji Spray 2203G Semi-PRO 2 Gravity HVLP Spray System

specs.controls: Fan pattern control, air control valve
specs.extras: 25 ft hose, 400cc gravity cup, metal turbine case, 2-year warranty

products.verdict: A real two-stage turbine HVLP system with a 25-foot hose and a gravity-feed gun. It's what finishers use for cabinets and furniture, and it rates 4.7 stars.
products.best_for: Cabinet painters and furniture finishers who want a smooth, sprayed finish.
products.skip_if: You just need to paint a fence once.
pros: Turbine stays on the floor; 25 ft hose

products.name: Fuji Spray 2202 Semi-PRO 2 HVLP Spray System

specs.controls: Fan pattern control, air control valve
specs.extras: 25 ft hose, 1 qt cup, metal turbine case

products.verdict: The same Fuji turbine as the 2203G with a 1-quart bottom-feed cup instead of a gravity cup, for longer runs between refills.
products.best_for: Finishers spraying larger pieces who want more paint in the cup.
products.skip_if: You spray at steep angles; the gravity 2203G is easier there.

products.name: Wagner Spraytech Control Spray Max Electric HVLP Paint Sprayer

specs.controls: Pressure dial, material flow adjuster, 3 patterns

products.verdict: A budget turbine-base HVLP with a two-stage turbine and a 20-foot hose, so the gun stays light. Wagner says it sprays thinned latex and thinner materials like stain and poly.
products.best_for: Furniture, doors and trim with a lighter gun than a handheld.
products.skip_if: You'll spray unthinned latex; it needs thinning.
pros: Turbine on the floor, 20 ft hose

products.name: Graco EVO Plus HVLP Paint and Stain Sprayer, Brass Nozzles
products.verdict: A Graco handheld with four solid brass nozzles (two for paint, two for stain) that sprays paint and stain straight from the can.
products.best_for: Cabinets, furniture, doors and trim without thinning.
products.skip_if: You want a long track record; it has 65 reviews and 4.1 stars.

products.name: Tilswall Shark 600 Ultra-Light HVLP Electric Paint Sprayer
products.verdict: A light, compact handheld that the listing says is 47% lighter than typical sprayers, with adjustable flow up to 1,200 mL per minute. Thin the paint for best results.
products.best_for: Small projects where a light sprayer matters.

products.name: PULENDY Paint Sprayer for House Painting, 4 Nozzles and 3 Spray Patterns
products.verdict: The cheapest sprayer here, much like the VONFORN: four nozzles, three patterns, a flow knob and a dust-blowing attachment.
products.best_for: One-off small projects like a planter or patio chairs.
products.skip_if: You'll paint a room; it's a light-duty sprayer.

products.name: Wagner Spraytech FLEXiO 4000 Stationary HVLP Paint and Stain Sprayer

specs.controls: Variable speed, adjustable flow, width and pattern
specs.extras: X-Boost turbine, 15 ft hose, 5 cup liners

products.verdict: Wagner's stationary version: the turbine sits on the floor with a 15-foot hose, and the X-Boost turbine sprays most unthinned latex and oil paints, primers and stains.
products.best_for: Bigger jobs like rooms, siding and fences where you want unthinned spraying without the weight in your hand.
products.skip_if: You want lots of owner reviews; it has 16.

avoid.name: 1000W HVLP Paint Sprayer, Electric Paint Gun with 1400ML Container, 4 Copper Nozzles and 3 Spray Patterns
avoid.flag: Placeholder model number and 1 x 1 inch dimensions
avoid.verdict: A generic four-nozzle sprayer whose listing data is placeholder text, so you can't trace the model, parts or support. The near-identical PULENDY and VONFORN sprayers cost less or the same.
reasons: The model number, model name and part number are all 'lqhs', and the spec table lists the sprayer's dimensions as 1 x 1 inch.
It claims a 1,000 W motor with no amp rating to back it, more than any other handheld here; VONFORN's similar design lists 700 W.
It's the same four-nozzle, three-pattern design as the VONFORN sprayer, which costs the same and has more than ten times the reviews.

buyers_guide.a: High volume, low pressure: a turbine blows lots of air at low pressure to atomize paint. You get less overspray and bounce-back than with airless sprayers, which makes HVLP good for furniture, cabinets and trim. It's slower than airless on whole houses.

buyers_guide.q: Do I have to thin the paint?
buyers_guide.a: With most handheld HVLPs, yes, especially for latex. Use the viscosity cup to check. Wagner's FLEXiO models and Graco's EVO Plus are sold as spraying unthinned paint with the right nozzle.

Handhelds put the motor and paint in your hand, which gets heavy. Turbine systems like the Fuji Semi-PRO and Wagner Control Spray Max keep the motor on the floor with a 15 to 25 foot hose, so the gun stays light and the air stays cooler and drier.
Expect 10 to 20 minutes: run water (or the right solvent) through the gun, then take the nozzle apart and brush it. Paint left to dry in the nozzle is the most common reason sprayers stop working.

buyers_guide.q: How do I avoid runs and orange peel?
buyers_guide.a: Practice on cardboard, keep the gun 6 to 10 inches away and moving, overlap each pass by half, and spray thin coats. Orange peel usually means paint too thick or too little air.
